guide.summary: Dropbox documents OAuth 2.0 bearer-token access for user-authorized API calls. The list_folder and list_folder/continue endpoints require files.metadata.read. The supplied sources do not document how to limit listing to the App Folder root or the production review and distribution rules, so those remain unknowns.

findings.title: Dropbox OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens authorize API requests
findings.detail: Dropbox supports OAuth 2.0 for authorizing API requests, sent as an Authorization Bearer header.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to per-customer authorization of the web app

evidence.quote: Dropbox supports OAuth 2.0
for authorizing API requests. Find out more in our OAuth guide . Authorized requests to the API should use an Authorization header with the value Bearer <TOKEN> , where <TOKEN>

findings.title: Authorization code flow uses the www.dropbox.com authorize URL and api.dropbox.com token endpoint
findings.detail: The authorize step uses www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize with client_id set to the app key; the code is exchanged at api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the code flow for an individual account

evidence.quote: URL Structure https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize Note: This is the only step that requires an endpoint on www.dropbox.com . All other API requests are done via api.dropboxapi.com , content.dropboxapi.com , or notify.dropboxapi.com .
curl https://api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token \ -d code= < AUTHORIZATION_COD E > \

findings.title: files.metadata.read is required to list folder entries
findings.detail: list_folder requires files.metadata.read and accepts a user OAuth token. The continuation endpoint uses the same scope.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to listing and continuing folder entries with a user token
